title: a re-export cycle that contains a reachable host-module edge still fails the pin, and the walk terminates
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin': the assertion is over the COMPLETE TRANSITIVE GRAPH, so a requirement reached through another module is the same requirement, and 'The diagnostic SHOULD show the dependency path that introduced the requirement.' `Module<"node:fs">` is poc/src/targets/classify.ts's concrete spelling of the JavaScript-host dependence that page names, and `blocksNativePin` refuses `TypeScript`, `Module<...>` and `Host<...>` together. `messageContains` pins the route because a pin refused with an empty route satisfies a code-and-position expectation exactly. The SMITHERS1510 companion lands in the auxiliary module, at the edge that reaches `node:fs`, because a re-export runs the target module's initializer exactly as an import does; it is declared rather than filtered because a cascade the language really does produce is part of the contract (conformance/README.md). The two auxiliary modules re-export from each other, so a walk that follows bindings has to detect the cycle. Terminating is not the whole obligation: the foreign edge inside the cycle is reachable and must still be charged, so this case distinguishes 'detected the cycle' from 'gave up inside it'. A run that never terminates is observed as a timeout rather than as a verdict, which is why the case pairs the route assertion with a program that is a cycle. RETIRED MARKER (go, 2026-08-23): the fork used to accept this program, grant the pin and print `9` — zero diagnostics where the reference reports SMITHERS1510@1:30 in cycle-a-host-module.mod.sm and SMITHERS3001@16:1 in the case. The fork now walks re-exports with a path-scoped visited stack (added before descending, deleted when the branch returns) so a cycle terminates without memoizing a clean answer for a namespace symbol (compiler/forkbridge/nativepin.go.txt). It distinguishes 'detected the cycle' from 'gave up inside it' the way this case requires: the run terminates AND the foreign edge inside the cycle is still charged, satisfying the declared route `-> cycle-b-host-module.mod.sm -> cycle-a-host-module.mod.sm -> node:fs`. Measured XPASS on go by `node conformance/runner/run.mjs --backend both --jobs 4`.
